name: graph-tool
why: Serious network analysis library with real graph theory depth, though it is a fairly standard research tool.

brief.what_it_is: graph-tool is an efficient Python module for manipulating and statistically analysing graphs (networks). You load or build a graph in Python, then run centrality, community detection, structural, and layout routines on it. The core data structures and algorithms are C++, so the Python API is a thin front end. The homepage also lists graph I/O (GraphML, GML, dot), a binary network format, filtered graph views, and drawing via cairo, GTK+, or graphviz.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as a fast alternative to Python-only network libraries, aimed at large-scale network analysis. It also offers inferential community detection that the author argues avoids the overfitting of off-the-shelf methods.
brief.how_it_works: Core data structures and algorithms are written in C++ using heavy template metaprogramming, built on the Boost Graph Library. Many algorithms are parallelised with OpenMP. Filtered graphs mask vertices and edges temporarily, and the homepage says this adds no performance cost when filtering is not used.

brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, the homepage lists Conda, Pixi, MacPorts, Arch, Debian/Ubuntu, Gentoo, Fedora and Docker routes. It also says bleeding-edge installs from the upstream repository are possible, with separate instructions. A Colab notebook is offered for a trial run without installing. The homepage links to a more detailed installation page, which I did not fetch. The brew caveats supplied with this entry add that drawing needs extra formulae (gtk+3, py3cairo, pygobject3, python-matplotlib) and that zstd decompression needs PYTHONPATH pointed at the bundled package under libexec; I did not verify these on the homepage.
brief.standout: Most network libraries are pure Python or thin wrappers. This one puts a Boost-based C++ core under a Python API and ships statistically principled inferential community detection and network reconstruction from dynamics, which few comparable packages offer. Filtered graphs that every function accepts at no cost when unused are also unusual.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage lists 3.9 as the newest version and links a changelog, but shows no release date, and I did not check the repository or changelog. It describes itself as mature, with more than 15 years on the cutting edge of network science.
brief.caveats: The homepage does not state platform limits. The Homebrew formula is a packaging layer over the upstream project, which has its own install routes. Graph drawing and zstd support need extra setup (from the supplied brew caveats). LGPLv3 licence, so check your own distribution terms. Performance claims are the author's; the homepage links a comparison I did not read.
quotes: Graph-tool is mature software that has been on the cutting edge of network science for more than 15 years.

Contrary to most other Python modules with similar functionality, the core data structures and algorithms are implemented in C++, making extensive use of template metaprogramming, based heavily on the Boost Graph Library.
Every single function in the module is documented in the docstrings and in the online documentation, which is full of examples.
fetch_log: https://graph-tool.skewed.de/ - fetched OK; returned the homepage text (not a GitHub README), which covered the description, features, install list, and demos. Did not follow the linked quick start, FAQ, or install pages, since the homepage was enough for this brief.
